questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Many friends had talked nicely about Bologna before. It was in Italy, that I like a lot. It is a famous old university and it is a very study friendly city close to nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a nice tutoring group if you wanted to know about social life, but the webpage of unibo is complicated and it is almost impossible to figure out where to go to talk to someone. Once the classes started all the professor were nice to talk to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy, but expensive. I could ask friends who had already been in Bologna.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The city is really small and the university is scattered, so don't bother try to live at the campus. Doesn't make sense. Don't even know if there is one.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think that it is really cool that you can sign up after some of the classes have started. So you can so to speak join the introduction lecture to see if you liked it and then you can pick after that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online webpage and then at rare times you could get a phone call to someone. Didn't help much though.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Please just get pre approval to all the courses that you could possibly think of taking and then shop around the introductory lectures to see what you like. But it is important to get the pre approval otherwise it is a little tedious to do the 'shopping'

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Chill exam. You could get away with a lazy attitude, but if you wanted to dive in and learn a lot that was definitely also possible. Very much up to you. High quality teachers in econ.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much smaller classes, much more interaction with the students. It was really nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Writing a research proposal in health economics
Development economics (with Paolo Masella, micro perspectives)
Economics of Regulation (Nicola Lacetera, favourite professor, about economic effects of AI). 

Critiques of Contemporary Capitalism (not an econ course)
English for Journalism (wouldn't recommend, I didn't learn anything)
Python for economist (wouldn't recommend either, but didn't go that much)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None of them really, but I do like Nicola Lacetera very much.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, but Bologna is very well connected by train. It can be expensive if you wanna go everywhere that you can go because it's so easy.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was really expensive. Groceries were also quite expensive compared to my expectations. Drinks, coffee and restaurants are cheap. 2-5 euros for a spritz / beer, coffe is 1,5 euro and a primi piatta is 8-10 euro if you go the right places.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Enjoying the hiking possiblities and the nature next to Bologna. I'm gonna miss that so much.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The hills. Take trains further away into the hills, so you don't only see the beginning of them. If you're there in the spring semester I would very highly recommend going to Monte Sole for the celebration at the 25. of April. Go there early. It is a really big experience and very beautiful. Go to lunch at LaBas.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine. So many internationals, but the italians were really nice to. Very open, the ones I met at least.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything that I remember

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very chill and laid back atmosphere. I loved the heavy rebellious energy and the demonstrations.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Text Laif Sardini for housing, it's safe social and easy, but quite expensive. 
Get pre-approval to aaaaall the courses that you could imagine taking and the do the 'intro class shopping'
Don't invite too many friends on visits. You're gonna want to indulge in your new life with your new friends. Visits are nice, but your friends are still there when you get home and it's tough being a host and being drawn away from all the exciting things that you can experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to Biblioteca Amilcar Cabral!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met some really nice people and I spent a long time a Biblioteca Amilcar Cabral and got to learn that place really well. That made me happy.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of different things on my mind regarding the future. Try not to think to much about that and just chill in Bolo

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
